text:
kiran: FYI noticed weird queue-depth jitter on the us-east gpu pool over the last 30m. 95th queue depth jumps between 40-120 tokens every ~3m.
ashley: seen that too. saw a spike in kube liveness probe failures around the same time :thinking: could be network-related.
devon: any related node churn or autoscaler events?
kiran: autoscaler shows very few scale events. node_provisioning_rate is flat. interestingly, gpu_utilization stayed moderate ~55%.
maria: I correlated with CNI metrics — `cni_tx_errors` and `pod_network_reconnects` spiked during the same windows. could be transient ENI/azure-vnet issues.
ashley: hmm, that would cause short periods where requests pile up -> larger batch sizes -> longer queues. did we see batch_size change?
kiran: yes. mean batch_size jumps from 4->12 during jitter intervals, and avg batch_latency climbs from 30ms -> 180ms.
ashley: can you paste the PromQL you used to correlate queue depth + probe failures?
kiran: sure:
```
sum by(cluster) (queue_depth{pool="us-east-gpus"})
/
sum by(cluster) (avg_over_time(kube_liveness_probe_failures[5m]))
```
(devon: note — that division is naive, I was just quick-checking co-occurrence)
opsbot: alert: us-east-gpus queue_depth_95pct above 80 triggered at 1812345630 — suppress window 5m.
maria: suggestion: add a short debounce in the queue-depth alert (10m window with 3m for-each) and surface correlated network probe panel in the same dashboard. saves noisy pages and gives context. :+1:
ashley: Agreed. Also propose a derived panel: "Batch size vs probe errors" as a heatmap so SREs can visually link batch spikes to network errors.
devon: we should also check kube-probe timeout values — there was a recent change in probe timeout from 1s -> 500ms in the node-launcher chart last week. if probes are too aggressive they amplify transient network blips into failure events.
kiran: opened a quick PR to increase probe timeout to 2s in node-launcher. will roll canary in staging first.
maria: for dashboards, here's a compact PromQL to show co-occurrence window: 
```
max_over_time(queue_depth{pool="us-east-gpus"}[10m]) > 80 and increase(kube_liveness_probe_failures[10m]) > 0
```
ashley: nice. Also add node-level ENI exhaustion metric and k8s API server latencies to the 'root cause' row.
opsbot: deployment: node-launcher chart v2.3.1-canary deployed to staging at 1812345700.
devon: ops question — does Dedicated have the same CNI config? we should check if customers on dedicated experience the same.
kiran: quick look — dedicated pools use our managed-cni v1.8 (older), hosted uses v1.9. different. might explain an AZ-specific incident.
maria: next steps: 1) debounce alert, 2) add correlated panels (probe failures, cni_tx_errors, eni_alloc_failures), 3) canary probe-timeout bump in staging, 4) run short load test to validate batch-size behavior.
ashley: I'll take dashboard updates. kiran please link the PR here when canary looks stable.
kiran: will do. thanks all :eyes:
thread_summary: short thread about queue-depth jitter in us-east GPU pool correlating with kube probe failures and CNI/networking blips; action items: alert debounce, dashboard panels, probe timeout canary, load test
